output.summary: KEP-2033 proposes running all Kubernetes node components (kubelet, CRI, OCI, CNI, kube-*) as a non-root user inside a user namespace, with small kubelet and kube-proxy changes to ignore sysctl and rlimit errors. Its status is implementable, stage beta, from 2021-05-24.
output.rationale: The main motivation is protecting the host from container-breakout vulnerabilities, and letting shared-machine users (HPC) and kind-style setups run Kubernetes without root. The authors argue admission hooks cannot mitigate vulnerabilities in kubelet, CRI, and OCI themselves, and that Node-level UserNS does not cover them. Reviewers accepted the approach but required a feature gate and documented caveats, and raised conformance-profile questions before beta.

alternatives.option: Node-level user namespaces (KEP-127), running only containers in a user namespace
alternatives.why_not: The readme says it "can't mitigate vulnerabilities of kubelet, CRI, OCI, and their relevant components" and that it is "out of scope for this KEP"; the two can be stacked.

alternatives.option: Kubelet externalized admission hooks to block pods requesting host privileges
alternatives.why_not: The author argues "Admission hooks are not efficient to mitigate vulnerabilities of the node components themselves (kubelet, CRI, OCI...)".

alternatives.option: Defer rootless until cgroup v2 and user namespace support (KEP-127) are finished
alternatives.why_not: Reviewer ehashman put a hold on the PR citing this dependency, but the author disagreed: "#127 is for running pods in UserNS, while this KEP is for running all the node components in UserNS." The sources do not show a final resolution of this hold beyond the later approval.

alternatives.option: Run rootless only outside the main repository as a proof of concept
alternatives.why_not: Raised by derekwaynecarr as a concern about long-term support; the author replied the work was already happening in the usernetes repo, but the KEP was still proposed for upstream merge.

evidence.quote: This KEP allows running the entire Kubernetes components (`kubelet`, CRI, OCI, CNI, and all `kube-*`) as a non-root user on the host, by running them in a user namespace.
The primary drawback of this KEP is its complexity. It also heavily relies on third-party, out-of-tree components.
There is an experiment to remove slirp overhead by using `SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_ADDFD` (Kernel 5.9)
to move to beta, we need clarity if we intend to define two separate types of conformance suites
SIG-release approved this in v1.22 milestone, with the merge deadline May 25.
